name: Saint Boniface
history: An English monk from Wessex, born Wynfrith, who became the Apostle of Germany. He felled the sacred oak of Donar at Geismar, organised the Church across the German lands as archbishop of Mainz, and founded the abbey of Fulda. In old age he returned to Frisia as a missionary and was martyred at Dokkum with his companions.
life: Wynfrith was given to the monastery at Exeter as a boy and later taught at Nursling near Southampton, where he wrote a Latin grammar. In 716 he sailed for Frisia, but war closed the mission. In Rome Pope Gregory II gave him the name Boniface and a commission to preach in Germany. At Geismar in Hesse he took an axe to the oak sacred to the thunder god, and when nothing befell him many were baptised; tradition says he built a chapel from its wood. He drew monks and nuns from England to help him, among them Saint Lioba, founded dioceses and held reforming synods for the Frankish Church. Past seventy he went back to Frisia. On 5 June 754, at Dokkum, a band of raiders fell on his camp. Tradition holds that he raised a book of the Gospels over his head as the blow fell.
prayerTo: Saint Boniface, you left England to carry the Gospel to the peoples beyond the sea, and you never stopped being a missionary. Pray for England and Germany, for all who bring the faith to new places, and for me, that I may not be afraid to cut down the idols in my own life. Amen.
penance: Write to, pray for or support a missionary today, and give up one comfort as an offering for the Church in Europe.
meditation: He was nearly eighty when he set out for Frisia again. Is there a work for God you have decided you are too old or too tired for?
prayer: O God, Who, through the zeal of blessed Boniface, Your Martyr and Bishop, graciously called a multitude of people to the knowledge of Your name, mercifully grant that we who keep his feast may also enjoy his patronage. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
